title: Autonomous System Observability, OpenTelemetry Tracing & Client-Side Real-User Monitoring (RUM) (Web Vitals, Distributed Tracing, Error Boundary Reporting)
spec:
# DIR-037: Autonomous System Observability, OpenTelemetry Tracing & Client-Side Real-User Monitoring (RUM)

## 1. Executive Context & Objectives (Enhancement Mandate)
Operating an enterprise-grade SaaS platform requires deep real-time visibility into distributed performance, API latencies, frontend errors, and Core Web Vitals. Relying solely on basic console logs or manual debugging is insufficient for production SLA guarantees.

This directive establishes a 10/10 **Autonomous System Observability & RUM Architecture**, introducing client-side Web Vitals tracking, structured JSON logging, distributed OpenTelemetry trace context propagation, React Error Boundary telemetry capture, and an Admin Observability dashboard.

## 2. Architecture Directives
1. **Client-Side Real-User Monitoring (RUM)**:
   - Capture Core Web Vitals (FCP, LCP, CLS, INP, TTFB) using standard web-vitals library.
   - Batch and buffer performance telemetry on the client and dispatch via navigator.sendBeacon to /api/telemetry/rum without affecting main thread performance.
   - Global Error Boundary in React: Capture uncaught exceptions, stack traces, active route, user role, and browser user-agent, sending sanitized crash reports to /api/telemetry/errors.

2. **Distributed Tracing & Server Telemetry**:
   - Express middleware injecting X-Correlation-ID / traceparent header into all incoming HTTP requests.
   - Propagate trace ID through database queries, AI provider invocations, and external payment gateway calls.
   - Measure and log: Route execution time, MariaDB query latency, AI model token generation speed, and external API response times.

3. **Platform Health & Metrics Telemetry Endpoint**:
   - Route: /api/admin/system/metrics and /health.
   - Report: Node.js event loop lag, memory usage (RSS, heapUsed), active database connections, Redis hit rate, and AI provider status.

4. **Admin Observability Dashboard View**:
   - Live visual charts in Admin System Console: Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99), error rate spikes, Web Vitals health scorecards, and recent error log viewer with filtering.

## 3. Acceptance Criteria
1. Client-side RUM captures Web Vitals and dispatches non-blocking beacons to backend.
2. React Error Boundary captures frontend exceptions with stack traces and displays an elegant Cuba M3 fallback UI with reload button.
3. Every API request receives a unique correlation ID present in response headers and server log entries.
4. Health check endpoint /health returns comprehensive status in under 20ms.
5. Admin Observability dashboard displays live p95 latency charts, error trends, and system metrics.
6. Zero PII or plaintext secret tokens logged in any telemetry payload.

## 4. Strict Invariants
1. Telemetry reporting must never crash or block user interface execution or API responses.
2. Sanitize all error logs: scrub passwords, JWT tokens, credit card numbers, and candidate PII.
3. Telemetry buffering must respect network offline state and drop payloads when storage exceeds bounds.
4. Maintain sub-5ms overhead for server-side tracing middleware.
invariants: Telemetry dispatch must be non-blocking and have zero impact on user experience
Strict automated scrubbing of all PII, secrets, and auth tokens from error logs
Health check endpoint must execute in < 20ms and require zero authentication
Admin telemetry dashboards must enforce SuperAdmin role authorization
acceptanceCriteria: Client RUM captures and dispatches Core Web Vitals seamlessly via sendBeacon
React Error Boundary provides graceful user recovery and automated diagnostic capture
Distributed correlation IDs propagate across all API requests and logs
Admin Observability console renders live latency charts and error inspection feeds
Sanitization pipeline verified: zero PII or credentials in logs
